title: Stage-Gate Variant Assayer: cohorted safety gates, per-request scoring, and auto-stop
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Ship a lightweight A/B-style experimentation primitive (the "Assayer") that runs short-lived comparisons between model versions with: cohorted exposure control, per-request risk scoring, sequential statistical checks, and automatic stop/rollback actions. This primitive will be exposed in the Console as a templated experiment workflow and as API-first controls for infra-driven flows.

Why: Current rollout tooling supports static weight canaries and long-running experiments but lacks: (1) per-request heuristics to flag quality risk earlier, (2) cohort-specific budgets (e.g., VIPs vs random sample) and (3) built-in sequential stopping that can act without manual intervention. The Assayer is intended for fast validation of model deltas with low blast radius and clear decision automation.

Scope & Non-goals:
- In scope: experiment definition API, sample allocation rules (cohorts + holdouts), per-request heuristic scoring module (latency, token-delta, safety-signal proxies), sequential statistical engine (optional SPRT or Bayesian sequential test), console UI for quick run + rollout decision, auto-stop and optional rollback hooks to routing.
- Out of scope (initial): full ML-quality eval suite (offline human labels), long-duration A/B dashboards, multi-arm experiments beyond binary comparisons.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Create experiment that splits traffic by cohort (named groups) with separate exposure budgets and per-cohort early-stop triggers.
2) Per-request scoring returns a small JSON of safety/quality proxies within 30ms median on hosted flow.
3) Sequential engine supports configurable thresholds (alpha/beta) and 3 stopping rules: superiority, inferiority, and futility.
4) Console shows live experiment view with cohorted exposures, stop reason, and link to the roll-forward/rollback action.
5) Auto-stop triggers a webhook that modifies routing weights (or marks variant inactive) and writes an incident-style entry to the experiments timeline.

Design decisions & trade-offs considered:
- Statistics: SPA (SPRT) gives quickest stops on strong signals; Bayesian sequential offers richer posterior info. We'll ship SPRT-first for deterministic behavior and add Bayesian mode in v2.
- Scoring: Use fast heuristics (model perplexity delta on short probes, hallucination proxy via keyword/NER mismatch, latency/cost delta) to avoid human-in-the-loop labels. These are noisy but allow early detection; we will require a post-mortem workflow to validate false positives.
- Exposure budgets: Cohorts get independent budgets to protect high-value users (VIPs) and production cohorts. Simpler central budget would be easier to implement but less flexible.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) API: POST /experiments to create binary comparison + cohort allocations + sequential settings.
2) Scoring service: lightweight lambda container invoked synchronously in the request path (prefetch probes + compute heuristics). Deploy to hosted plane with fast path optimization.
3) Stats engine: standalone service that ingests scored events and emits evaluation decisions via pubsub.
4) Router integration: feature-flag-style switch controlled by experiment state; auto-stop webhook flips flag.
5) Console: experiment builder, live cohort view, and action buttons (stop/extend/rollback).

Telemetry & observability:
- Per-experiment metrics: samples per cohort, stopping probability, cumulative reward deltas, latency distribution, hallucination proxy rate, token-cost delta.
- Audit logs: every auto-stop or weight change must be auditable with experiment snapshot.
- Post-run artifacts: exportable csv of scored events and final test statistic.

Risks & mitigations:
- False positives from heuristics -> mitigation: require two independent signals OR thresholded secondary check before rollback.
- Performance overhead -> mitigation: sampling (only score X% of requests) + async fallback for non-critical probes.
- Customer trust (auto-rollback) -> mitigation: enterprise opt-in for auto-rollback, mandatory notification channel + manual-confirm fallback for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Rollout plan:
- Alpha: internal infra teams + 3 partner product teams (low-latency chat, docs summarization) -> collect ops signal and false-positive rate.
- Beta: enable via feature flag for all hosted accounts with safe default (no auto-rollback).
- GA: auto-rollback enabled for accounts after acceptance and documented guardrails.
